answer.location_description: Small 3x3 square near the top-left corner of the image (rows 1-3, columns 1-3), framed by a negatively weighted border at row 0, column 0, row 4 and column 4.
answer.shortcut_type: bright square marker/patch artifact in corner
answer.mechanism: Two groups of first-layer units detect the patch. The first group (units 0, 1, 2, 8, 18, 20, 29) has large negative biases and about +60 to +99 weights on the 3x3 patch, so these units turn on when the patch is bright. They feed strongly positively into layer-2 units u3 and u10 (e.g. u10 weights 89, 99, 77, 74, 73), which have positive output weights (+65, +64). The second group (units 9, 21, 24, 27) has large positive biases and about -60 to -80 weights on the patch, so a bright patch switches them off. These units drive layer-2 units u0, u6, u8 and u15 (weights about +40 to +70), which have large negative output weights (-90, -99, -82, -89). Turning them off removes negative evidence. Both pathways push the logit toward malignant when the corner patch is bright.
answer.evidence: The patch weights are by far the largest in W1 and form a sharp, uniform 3x3 block at r1-r3, c1-c3 (e.g. unit 29: 83 83 85 / 79 85 84 / 75 84 99; unit 24: -62 -58 -75 / -65 -70 -77 / -67 -67 -80). The block is surrounded by an opposite-sign frame (row 0, column 0, row 4, column 4 around -20 to -39 for the positive units and +20 to +43 for the negative units). This is a template for a bright square on a dark background in a corner of the 30 mm crop, which is not a nodule or lung property. The same 11 units carry large matched biases (-61 to -91, or +73 to +99), and their signs route consistently through layer 2 to raise the logit. The remaining units (3-7, 10-17, 19, 22, 23, 25, 26, 28, 30, 31) contain only small noise weights.
answer.main_feature: Genuine signal is centered on the nodule: the patch-detecting units also carry a centre-surround pattern, with opposite-sign weights on the central nodule pixels (rows 11-13, cols 10-13) and a ring of the opposite sign around it, plus a lower lobe at rows 19-21. Units 2 and 20 add broad positive weights over the field, reflecting overall soft-tissue density. Together these encode nodule size, density and margin.
